value.description_html:
A striking piece of American wartime public service history, this USDA Forest Service poster from the mid-1940s captures the urgent national campaign to prevent forest fires during World War II. The bold composition features an oversized hand crushing out a cigarette on a woodland rock, a direct visual instruction that needed no translation. The flame-styled lettering of 'PREVENT FOREST FIRES!' adds visceral urgency to the message.

Produced by the U.S. Government Printing Office for joint distribution by the federal Forest Service and state forestry agencies, this poster predates the now-iconic Smokey Bear by mere months. During the war years, America's forests were considered strategic resources essential for shipbuilding and military construction, while the genuine threat of Japanese incendiary balloon attacks made civilian fire prevention a matter of national security.

A compelling document of the home front effort, this poster bridges wartime anxiety with environmental stewardship in a way that resonates across decades. A standout piece for collectors of WWII Americana, conservation history, or mid-century graphic design.

Size: 20.0" x 14.25"

Artist: Baldridge

Condition: Very Good, Condition: Very Good, Age-appropriate wear, fading and toning. Original fold lines present. Circle drawn on backside of upper right corner, lightly visible on front. Creasing in upper right corner. Light border wear. Please use the photo zoom feature to get a better understanding of overall condition. *Additional photos available upon request.

products.description_html:
Constantin Alajalov captures the electric energy of a Harlem nightclub in this stunning late 1920s illustration. The Russian-American artist, celebrated for his sophisticated magazine work, renders the scene with his characteristic Art Deco elegance: elongated chorus girls in coral-fringed costumes ascend the stage in synchronized movement, while a central couple commands the spotlight in an intimate dance.

The composition brilliantly conveys the theatrical atmosphere of Jazz Age Harlem, where legendary venues drew adventurous audiences seeking the pulse of American nightlife. Alajalov's masterful handling of dramatic lighting, with cool spotlight beams cutting through warm amber tones, creates a sense of glamour and intrigue that defined the era.

A remarkable document of the Harlem Renaissance at its height, this illustration embodies the cultural ferment that made uptown Manhattan the center of American creative life. Signed by the artist in the lower right, this piece represents both exceptional artistic achievement and significant cultural history.

Size: 13.5" x 10"

Artist: Constantin Alajalov

Condition: Very Good, Age-appropriate wear. Paper toning in accordance with the print's age. Marks/stains as per photo. Wear around the edges and minor paper loss might be present in some prints. Some illustrations may have writing or images on verso. Please refer to each print's image to get a better understanding of the condition.

products.description_html:
This George Petty illustration epitomizes the sophisticated glamour that defined American magazine art during the mid-1930s. Signed 'PETTY' in the upper left, the piece showcases his signature airbrush technique: luminous flesh tones, a dramatic orange-red backdrop, and the diaphanous oversized hat that became a recurring Petty motif. The figure, telephone pressed to her ear, embodies the flirtatious wit that made the Petty Girl a cultural phenomenon.

The suggestive caption ('Well, we could go to the opera, Mr. Hammond, if you insist on preliminaries') captures the playful sophistication Esquire cultivated during the Depression era, offering readers escapist fantasy with a knowing wink. Petty's technical virtuosity is on full display: the seamless color gradients, the translucent fabric effects, and the idealized proportions that influenced generations of illustrators.

A standout piece for collectors of Golden Age illustration, pin-up art, or vintage Americana, this Petty original bridges fine art technique with popular culture impact.

Size: 12.75" x 9"

Artist: George Petty

Condition: Very Good, Age-appropriate wear. Paper toning in accordance with the print's age. Marks/stains as per photo. Wear around the edges and minor paper loss might be present in some prints. Some illustrations may have writing or images on verso. Please refer to each print's image to get a better understanding of the condition.

collections.description_html: This range tends to be where genuine variety lives. Period works at this price point span formats and eras, from late 19th-century commercial illustration to mid-century travel and entertainment posters to original psychedelic concert work from the 1960s. Condition, rarity, and format all shift the value, so the mix at any moment reflects what the market actually produces. Everything here is a period original, not a modern facsimile.

This price range tends to bring in work with a real track record: pieces old enough to carry genuine historical weight, by artists or from movements that have held collector interest over time. Lithographed advertising posters from the early 20th century sit comfortably here, as do rare printed ephemera from the 19th century. The period originals in this range are the kind of work that rewards closer attention the longer it hangs on a wall.

This range tends to be where genuine variety opens up: travel posters, foreign film releases, concert work, and more, spanning the mid-20th century through the 1980s. Period originals at this level often reflect regional printing traditions that don't survive in large numbers, whether a Japanese studio release or a European travel commission. The works here are period originals, not modern reproductions.

At this level, the market narrows to works with genuine art-historical weight: large-format lithographs from the Belle Époque, interwar commercial masterworks by designers like Cassandre, and rare concert posters from the psychedelic era. These are pieces that defined their genres rather than followed them. Period originals at this price reflect condition, rarity, and the kind of provenance that serious collectors and institutions look for.

This range tends to attract serious work from the mid-20th century golden age of commercial illustration, when travel, cinema, and consumer brands all competed for wall space through hand-drawn imagery. Designers like Edward McKnight Kauffer and Milton Glaser brought genuine artistic ambition to commercial commissions, and their period work sits comfortably here alongside lesser-known but equally skilled hands. All are period originals, not modern reproductions.

products.description_html:
Originally designed in 1969 for The Who's three night engagement at Detroit's legendary Grande Ballroom, this classic Carl Lundgren image was later reissued as a signed and numbered artist edition limited to 200 copies. The composition captures one of Lundgren's most dynamic concert poster designs, centering on a cosmic explosion from which musical instruments, lightning bolts, hands, and abstract forms radiate outward, a fitting visual metaphor for The Who's electrifying live performances at the height of their late 1960s career.

Lundgren's distinctive style bridges underground comix and psychedelic poster art, while the lower panels function as a visual program guide for the weekend's supporting acts: Joe Cocker and the Grease Band on Friday, Mixed Generation on Saturday, and Rush, the Detroit group rather than the later Canadian trio, on Sunday. A vibrant palette of purples, blues, and turquoise gives the composition a graphic intensity that has become synonymous with the Grande Ballroom series.

Printed by The Highway Press, this artist authorized edition preserves one of Lundgren's most celebrated Grande Ballroom designs while commemorating both Detroit's influential rock scene and one of The Who's memorable American performances during the band's formative years.

Size: 29.0" x 18.0"

Condition: Very Good, Age-appropriate wear, fading and toning. Light border wear. Please use the photo zoom feature to get a better understanding of overall condition. *Additional photos available upon request.
